(Satyam Jaiswal Vs The State Of Madhya Pr
 Dated : 08-11-2024
 Shri Prahlad Choudhary - Advocate for the appellant.

Ms. Supriya Singh - Deputy Government 
 respondent/State.

Heard on I.A. No. 29064/2023, which is second bail application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C.
for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

The appellant has been convicted under Section 363 of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 3 years and fine of Rs. 1000/-, Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 3 years and fine of Rs.
1000/- and Section 376-D of IPC and sentenced to RI for 20 years and fine of Rs.3,000/- with default stipulations.
His first application was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 01.07.2023 (I.A.No.24203 of 2022).
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the instant case, appellant has been falsely implicated.
Learned trial court has not appreciated evidence properly.
It is urged that in the instant case, no DNA report has been filed and FSL report does not support the prosecution story.

After referring to para 9 of prosecutrix's testimony as well as MLC, it is also urged that looking to the place of incident, prosecutrix should have sustained some injuries but in MLC, no external and internal injuries have been found on the person of prosecutrix.

It is also urged that there are material contradictions in court testimony of prosecutrix and her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. Looking to the nature of incident, 2 CRA-9388-2022 prosecutix does not appear reliable witness.
Appeal is of 2022.
Appellant is in custody for more than 2 years.
There is no possibility of early hearing of this appeal in near future Thus, remaining jail sentence of appellant may be suspended.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the application.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After examining and taking into consideration the evidence on record, especially, deposition of prosecutrix, pre MLC, FSL report and absence of DNA report, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant.
Accordingly, I.A No. 29064/2023 is allowed.

Subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant-Satyam Jaiswal is hereby suspended and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court with a further direction to appear before the concerning trial court on 12.12.2024 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
C. c. as per rules.

(DWARKA DHISH BANSAL) (ACHA  JUDGE   L.R.
